lexemes.canonicalForm: ありがとうございます

forms.text: ありがとうございます

readings.text: ありがとうございます

grammar.label: です
grammar.summary: polite noun/adjective predicate ending
grammar.mentalModel: です politely presents a noun or adjective as the predicate of the sentence. It does not carry the same meaning as an English word-for-word 'is' in every construction.

grammar.label: は (topic)
grammar.summary: marks what the sentence is about
grammar.mentalModel: は sets a topic: 'as for X...'. The topic is discourse information, not automatically the grammatical subject.

grammar.label: か (question)
grammar.summary: marks a polite sentence as a question
grammar.mentalModel: In polite beginner sentences, final か turns the proposition into a question without requiring English-style word-order inversion.

grammar.label: 〜ます
grammar.summary: polite nonpast verb predicate
grammar.mentalModel: 〜ます is the polite nonpast verb form. Depending on context it can describe a present habit or a future action.

grammar.label: を (object)
grammar.summary: marks the direct object of an action
grammar.mentalModel: を marks the thing most directly affected by many transitive actions.

grammar.label: で (action place)
grammar.summary: marks the place where an action happens
grammar.mentalModel: で frames a location as the setting of an activity: the action happens there.

grammar.label: に (destination/location)
grammar.summary: marks a destination or existence location
grammar.mentalModel: に points to a target location. With movement it marks the destination; with ある/いる it marks where something exists.
formation: Place + に + X + が + あります/います

grammar.label: と (with)
grammar.summary: marks a companion in an action
grammar.mentalModel: と links a participant who does an action together with someone.

grammar.label: も (also)
grammar.summary: marks an additional parallel topic or participant
grammar.mentalModel: も adds an item to an already relevant set: 'X too / X also'.
uses: add another item with the same relation

grammar.label: が (subject/focus)
grammar.summary: marks a focused or newly presented subject
grammar.mentalModel: が marks a grammatical subject and often presents or focuses information that is not merely the established topic.

grammar.label: ある / いる
grammar.summary: expresses existence: ある for inanimate things, いる for animate beings
grammar.mentalModel: Japanese commonly describes existence with a location marked by に and the existing entity marked by が. ある is used for inanimate things; いる for people and animals.
formation: Place + に + Thing + が + あります
Place + に + Person/animal + が + います

grammar.label: 〜が好きです
grammar.summary: expresses liking with the liked thing marked by が
grammar.mentalModel: With 好き, the thing liked is commonly marked by が. Treat the whole pattern as a Japanese preference construction rather than mapping English 'like' word for word.

grammar.label: い-adjective + です
grammar.summary: polite descriptive predicate with an い-adjective
grammar.mentalModel: An い-adjective can itself be the predicate; adding です makes the sentence polite without turning the adjective into a noun.

grammar.label: 〜ません
grammar.summary: polite nonpast negative verb form
grammar.mentalModel: 〜ません is the polite negative counterpart of 〜ます. It says an action does not happen or will not happen.

grammar.label: 〜ました
grammar.summary: polite past affirmative verb form
grammar.mentalModel: 〜ました places a polite verb action in the completed past.

grammar.label: の (linking nouns)
grammar.summary: links one noun to another for possession, category or relationship
grammar.mentalModel: Think of の as attaching one noun as a label or relationship to the noun that follows. English may use 'of', possessive 's', or an attributive noun.

grammar.label: これ / それ / あれ
grammar.summary: points to a thing as this, that near the listener, or that over there
grammar.mentalModel: Japanese demonstratives encode distance from the speaker and listener. これ, それ and あれ stand on their own as pronouns.
formation: これ / それ / あれ + は ...

grammar.label: この / その / あの + noun
grammar.summary: points to a specific noun as this, that, or that over there
grammar.mentalModel: この, その and あの cannot stand alone; they directly modify a following noun.
formation: この / その / あの + Noun
uses: identifying a specific object or person

grammar.label: ここ / そこ / あそこ / どこ
grammar.summary: expresses here, there, over there, and where
grammar.mentalModel: Location demonstratives use the same distance system as これ / それ / あれ. どこ asks which location.
formation: ここ / そこ / あそこ + です

grammar.label: basic question words
grammar.summary: places an interrogative word in the information slot being asked about
grammar.mentalModel: Japanese usually keeps the normal sentence structure and replaces the unknown information with a question word such as だれ, どこ, いつ, どう, どれ or いくら.
uses: asking who, where, when, how, which, or how much

grammar.label: time + に
grammar.summary: marks a specific time when an event happens
grammar.mentalModel: Use に with clock times and other specific points in time. Relative time words such as 今日, 明日 and 昨日 commonly appear without に.

grammar.label: 〜から / 〜まで
grammar.summary: marks a starting point and an ending point
grammar.mentalModel: から sets a start and まで sets an end. They can describe time spans or physical ranges.
formation: Start + から + End + まで

grammar.label: で (means / transport)
grammar.summary: marks the means, tool or transport used for an action
grammar.mentalModel: The particle で can mark what is used to carry an action out, such as 電車で 'by train'. This is distinct from its action-location use.

grammar.label: と (complete noun list)
grammar.summary: connects nouns in a complete list
grammar.mentalModel: Between nouns, と works like a complete 'and' list. This differs from と marking a companion with an action.

grammar.label: 〜つ (general counter)
grammar.summary: counts many ordinary objects with the native Japanese counter series
grammar.mentalModel: Japanese uses counters rather than a single universal counting form. 〜つ is a broad beginner counter for many ordinary objects.
formation: 一つ / 二つ / 三つ ...

grammar.label: 〜人 (people counter)
grammar.summary: counts people with the 人 counter
grammar.mentalModel: The people counter has special beginner readings for one and two people: ひとり and ふたり. Higher numbers usually use 〜にん.
formation: 一人 / 二人 / 三人 ...

grammar.label: 〜時 / 〜分 / 半
grammar.summary: builds basic clock-time expressions
grammar.mentalModel: Hours use 時, minutes use 分 with sound changes after some numbers, and 半 adds 'half past'. Treat the clock expression as a compositional counter pattern.

grammar.label: 〜ませんでした
grammar.summary: polite past negative verb form
grammar.mentalModel: Attach ませんでした to the polite verb stem to say that an action did not happen.
formation: Verb stem + ませんでした

grammar.label: い-adjective negative
grammar.summary: makes an い-adjective negative with 〜くない
grammar.mentalModel: Remove the final い and add くない. Add です for ordinary polite speech. The common adjective いい uses the よい stem in its conjugated forms.
formation: 高い → 高くない(です)
いい → よくない(です)
uses: saying something is not expensive, big, cold, etc.

grammar.label: い-adjective past
grammar.summary: makes an い-adjective past with 〜かった
grammar.mentalModel: Remove the final い and add かった. Add です for polite speech. いい follows the よい stem: よかった.
formation: 高い → 高かった(です)
いい → よかった(です)

grammar.label: noun / な-adjective negative predicate
grammar.summary: uses じゃない(です) for a negative noun or な-adjective predicate
grammar.mentalModel: Nouns and な-adjectives share this predicate pattern: replace the affirmative copular ending with じゃない; です may be added in ordinary polite speech.

grammar.label: noun / な-adjective past predicate
grammar.summary: uses だった or でした for past noun and な-adjective predicates
grammar.mentalModel: For a polite past predicate use でした. The corresponding plain past form is だった.
formation: 学生でした / 学生だった
静かでした / 静かだった

grammar.label: verb て-form
grammar.summary: connects a verb to following grammar and serves as the base for many linked forms
grammar.mentalModel: The て-form is generated from the verb class. It is not a tense by itself; it links the verb to what follows and is reused by many later patterns.

grammar.label: 〜てください
grammar.summary: makes a polite request for someone to do an action
grammar.mentalModel: Attach ください to the て-form. The request is direct but standard and useful in classrooms, shops and everyday service situations.

grammar.label: Noun + をください
grammar.summary: politely asks for an item
grammar.mentalModel: With a noun, をください requests that item. This differs from verb て-form + ください, which requests an action.

grammar.label: ね (shared confirmation)
grammar.summary: invites agreement or checks shared understanding
grammar.mentalModel: Sentence-final ね frames a statement as something the speaker expects the listener can share, recognize or confirm.

grammar.label: よ (informing)
grammar.summary: marks information the speaker actively presents to the listener
grammar.mentalModel: Sentence-final よ highlights information the speaker is giving, pointing out or gently correcting for the listener.

grammar.label: 〜ている
grammar.summary: Express an action in progress, a repeated activity, or a resulting state.
grammar.mentalModel: The て-form connects the action to いる; context decides whether you are seeing 'is doing', a habitual activity, or a state that remains.
grammar.formation: Verb て-form + いる / います

practice.prompt: 今、音楽を聞い ___。
practice.explanation: 聞いています presents the listening as in progress now.

grammar.label: 〜たい
grammar.summary: Express the speaker's desire to do an action.
grammar.mentalModel: Attach たい to the verb's ます-stem. It behaves like an い-adjective.
grammar.formation: Verb ます-stem + たい
uses: asking what someone wants to do

practice.prompt: 映画を見 ___。
practice.explanation: 見たいです means 'I want to see/watch.'

grammar.label: 〜が欲しい
grammar.summary: Express wanting a thing.
grammar.mentalModel: 欲しい describes a desired noun; mark that desired thing with が in the basic pattern.
grammar.formation: Noun + が欲しい

practice.prompt: 新しい自転車 ___ 欲しいです。
practice.explanation: The desired item is marked by が with 欲しい.

grammar.label: 〜たことがある
grammar.summary: Talk about having or not having a past experience.
grammar.mentalModel: Turn the completed action into an experience with こと and state whether that experience exists.
grammar.formation: Verb plain past + ことがある / あります
uses: asking whether someone has ever done something

practice.prompt: 日本に行ったことが ___。
practice.explanation: 〜たことがあります reports past experience.

grammar.label: 〜ことができる
grammar.summary: Express ability or possibility to do an action.
grammar.mentalModel: Nominalize the action with こと and say that it is possible with できる.
grammar.formation: Verb dictionary form + ことができる

practice.prompt: 日本語でメールを書くことが ___。
practice.explanation: 〜ことができます means 'can do'.

grammar.label: 〜つもり
grammar.summary: State a deliberate intention.
grammar.mentalModel: つもり presents a plan as your current intention rather than merely a scheduled event.
grammar.formation: Verb dictionary/plain negative + つもりだ / です

practice.prompt: 来週、京都へ旅行する ___ です。
practice.explanation: 〜つもりです states a deliberate intention.

grammar.label: 〜予定
grammar.summary: State a scheduled or arranged plan.
grammar.mentalModel: 予定 frames an event as being on the schedule or already arranged.
grammar.formation: Verb dictionary form / Noun + の + 予定だ / です

practice.prompt: 週末は映画を見る ___ です。
practice.explanation: 〜予定です presents the action as scheduled.

grammar.label: 〜と思う
grammar.summary: Report what you think or believe.
grammar.mentalModel: Quote a plain-form proposition with と and attach 思う.
grammar.formation: Plain clause + と思う / 思います

practice.prompt: 日本語は面白い ___ 思います。
practice.explanation: と marks the content of the thought before 思います.

grammar.label: 〜から (reason)
grammar.summary: Give a direct reason for what follows.
grammar.mentalModel: Put から after the reason clause: 'because X, Y.'
grammar.formation: Reason clause + から

practice.prompt: 明日は会議がある ___、早く寝ます。
practice.explanation: Clause-final から gives the reason for the following action.

grammar.label: 〜ので
grammar.summary: Give a relatively explanatory or softer reason.
grammar.mentalModel: ので connects a reason to its consequence with a more explanatory tone than direct から.
grammar.formation: Plain clause + ので; Noun/な-adjective + なので

practice.prompt: 雨 ___、バスで行きます。
practice.explanation: 雨なので gives 'because it is raining/rainy' as background reason.

grammar.label: 〜けど / 〜が
grammar.summary: Connect two ideas with contrast or soften what follows.
grammar.mentalModel: The first clause sets up a contrast; the second clause gives the differing result or evaluation.
grammar.formation: Clause + けど / が

practice.prompt: この店は便利です ___、少し高いです。
practice.explanation: が can connect two clauses with 'but'.

grammar.label: 〜より〜のほうが
grammar.summary: Compare two things.
grammar.mentalModel: より marks the comparison baseline; ほう marks the side that has more of the stated quality.
grammar.formation: A より B のほうが + adjective

practice.prompt: バス ___ 電車のほうが速いです。
practice.explanation: より marks the baseline in a comparison.

grammar.label: 〜が一番
grammar.summary: Express the top choice or highest degree within a group.
grammar.mentalModel: 一番 means 'number one / most' in the relevant comparison set.
grammar.formation: Group + で / among context + Noun が一番 + adjective

practice.prompt: 季節では春が ___ 好きです。
practice.explanation: 一番 marks spring as the favorite/most liked.

grammar.label: 〜てもいい
grammar.summary: Ask for or give permission.
grammar.mentalModel: The て-form plus もいい presents the action as acceptable.
grammar.formation: Verb て-form + もいい

practice.prompt: ここで写真を撮っ ___ いいですか。
practice.explanation: 〜てもいいですか asks whether an action is permitted.

grammar.label: 〜てはいけない
grammar.summary: State that an action is prohibited.
grammar.mentalModel: The て-form plus はいけない marks the action as unacceptable.
grammar.formation: Verb て-form + はいけない / はいけません

practice.prompt: ここで食べ ___ いけません。
practice.explanation: 〜てはいけません means 'must not do'.

grammar.label: 〜なければならない
grammar.summary: Express obligation: something must be done.
grammar.mentalModel: Use the negative base and conditional なければ, then ならない: if it is not done, that will not do.
grammar.formation: Verb ない-form → なければならない

practice.prompt: 薬を飲ま ___ なりません。
practice.explanation: 〜なければなりません expresses 'must'.

grammar.label: 〜なくてもいい
grammar.summary: Express that an action is not necessary.
grammar.mentalModel: Negative なくて + もいい says it is okay even without doing the action.
grammar.formation: Verb ない-form → なくてもいい

practice.prompt: 今日は仕事に行か ___ いいです。
practice.explanation: 〜なくてもいい means 'do not have to'.

grammar.label: 〜てから
grammar.summary: Sequence actions: do one action and then another.
grammar.mentalModel: The first action is completed before the next one begins.
grammar.formation: Verb て-form + から

practice.prompt: 朝ご飯を食べ ___、学校に行きます。
practice.explanation: 〜てから explicitly orders the second action after the first.

grammar.label: 〜たり〜たりする
grammar.summary: Give representative examples of actions.
grammar.mentalModel: Use past-form-like たり on multiple verbs to present examples rather than a complete list.
grammar.formation: Verb past stem + り ... + する

practice.prompt: 映画を見 ___、買い物をし ___ します。
practice.explanation: Repeated 〜たり presents representative activities.

grammar.label: 〜前に / 〜後で
grammar.summary: Place one action before or after another.
grammar.mentalModel: 前 and 後 act as time anchors around an action or noun.
grammar.formation: Verb dictionary + 前に; Verb past / Noun の + 後で

practice.prompt: 寝る ___、薬を飲みます。
practice.explanation: 寝る前に means 'before going to bed'.

grammar.label: 〜ながら
grammar.summary: Do two actions at the same time.
grammar.mentalModel: Attach ながら to the ます-stem of the secondary action; the final verb is the main action.
grammar.formation: Verb ます-stem + ながら

practice.prompt: 音楽を聞き ___、料理します。
practice.explanation: 聞きながら means 'while listening'.

grammar.label: 〜くなる / 〜になる
grammar.summary: Express a change of state.
grammar.mentalModel: い-adjectives use 〜くなる; nouns and な-adjectives use 〜になる.
grammar.formation: い-adjective: 〜くなる; Noun/な-adjective: 〜になる

practice.prompt: 最近、忙し ___ なりました。
practice.explanation: い-adjectives change to 〜く before なる.

grammar.label: 〜にする
grammar.summary: Choose or intentionally make something into a state.
grammar.mentalModel: にする presents an intentional choice or change, unlike になる which describes becoming.
grammar.formation: Noun/な-adjective + にする

practice.prompt: 飲み物はお茶 ___ します。
practice.explanation: お茶にします means 'I'll choose/have tea.'

grammar.label: 〜すぎる
grammar.summary: Say that something is excessive.
grammar.mentalModel: Attach すぎる to a verb stem or adjective stem: too much / too X.
grammar.formation: Verb ます-stem + すぎる; い-adj stem + すぎる; な-adj + すぎる

practice.prompt: このかばんは重 ___。
practice.explanation: 重すぎます means 'it is too heavy.'

grammar.label: 〜やすい / 〜にくい
grammar.summary: Describe how easy or difficult an action is to do.
grammar.mentalModel: Attach やすい or にくい to the verb's ます-stem.
grammar.formation: Verb ます-stem + やすい / にくい

practice.prompt: この本は読み ___。
practice.explanation: 読みやすい means 'easy to read.'

grammar.label: 〜ませんか
grammar.summary: Make a polite invitation.
grammar.mentalModel: A polite negative question can function as an invitation: 'won't you...?'
grammar.formation: Verb ます-stem + ませんか

practice.prompt: 一緒に昼ご飯を食べ ___。
practice.explanation: 〜ませんか politely invites the listener.

grammar.label: 〜たら
grammar.summary: Express a practical if/when condition.
grammar.mentalModel: Attach ら to the plain past form. In many everyday contexts it means 'if/when X happens, then Y.'
grammar.formation: Verb/adjective plain past + ら

practice.prompt: 駅に着い ___、電話してください。
practice.explanation: 着いたら means 'when/if you arrive.'

grammar.label: 〜とき
grammar.summary: Say when something happens.
grammar.mentalModel: Place とき after a plain-form clause or noun phrase to create a time frame.
grammar.formation: Plain clause + とき; Noun + のとき

practice.prompt: 道が分からない ___、駅で聞きます。
practice.explanation: 〜とき means 'when...'.

grammar.label: もう / まだ
grammar.summary: Locate an event relative to an expected point: already, still, or not yet.
grammar.mentalModel: もう often marks a change already reached; まだ marks a state continuing or something not yet completed.
grammar.formation: もう + affirmative; まだ + affirmative/negative depending meaning

practice.prompt: 宿題は ___ 終わっていません。
practice.explanation: まだ〜ていません means 'not yet'.

canDos.statement: Can identify oneself or another person with a simple polite noun predicate.
Can ask and answer a simple personal-information question.
Can state simple everyday actions and their direct objects.
Can say where an action happens and where someone is going.
Can say who an action is done with and add a parallel person or item.
Can say that a person or thing exists at a location.
Can express a simple preference and describe something with a basic adjective.
Can contrast affirmative, negative and past polite actions in a simple routine.
Can point out and identify nearby or visible things with basic demonstratives.
Can ask and answer where something is and identify a person or item with basic question words.
Can express simple possession or noun relationships and list two items.
Can tell a basic clock time and state when an activity starts, happens, or ends.
Can describe a simple daily routine and say that a past action did not happen.
Can describe people, places, weather and things in affirmative, negative and past forms.
Can identify close family members and state a simple family size or location.
Can order a simple food or drink item and request a small quantity politely.
Can ask a price, understand a simple yen amount, and request a basic quantity while shopping.
Can say how to travel to a place and understand basic left/right location language.
Can request repetition or slower speech and signal that something was not understood.
Can sustain a short polite exchange using confirmation, new-information marking, yes/no responses and a few question words.
Can describe what people are doing, where they live, and ongoing routines.
Can talk about personal intentions and scheduled plans.
Can say what one has experienced and what one is able to do.
Can say what one wants and make a simple invitation.
Can explain a reason, contrast ideas, and state a simple opinion.
Can compare two things and state a favorite within a group.
Can ask whether something is allowed and understand a basic prohibition.
Can say what must be done and what does not need to be done.
Can describe sequences, representative activities, and simultaneous actions.
Can describe changes and choose among simple options.
Can say that something is too much, easy to do, or difficult to do.
Can respond to common travel or daily-life problems with simple conditions and situation language.

readingTexts.title: A school morning
readingTexts.description: Follow a simple morning routine from waking up to bedtime.

comprehensionQuestions.prompt: What time does the person get up?
comprehensionQuestions.explanation: 毎日七時に起きます says the person gets up at seven every day.

comprehensionQuestions.prompt: Where does the person study Japanese?
comprehensionQuestions.explanation: 学校で日本語を勉強します places the studying at school.

readingTexts.title: My family
readingTexts.description: Read a compact family introduction with roles and locations.

comprehensionQuestions.prompt: How many people are in the family?
comprehensionQuestions.explanation: 私の家族は四人です states that the family has four people.

comprehensionQuestions.prompt: Who is a company employee?
comprehensionQuestions.explanation: 母は会社員です says the mother is a company employee.

readingTexts.title: At a small shop
readingTexts.description: Move through a beginner shopping exchange with prices, quantities and food.

comprehensionQuestions.prompt: What price is stated?
comprehensionQuestions.explanation: 三百円です means 'It is 300 yen.'

comprehensionQuestions.prompt: How many apples are requested?
comprehensionQuestions.explanation: りんごを三つください requests three apples.

readingTexts.title: Finding the station
readingTexts.description: Combine directions and transport language into one short route.

comprehensionQuestions.prompt: Where is the station?
comprehensionQuestions.explanation: 駅はあそこですよ points out that the station is over there.

comprehensionQuestions.prompt: Which vehicle is used to go to the station?
comprehensionQuestions.explanation: バスで駅に行きます means 'I go to the station by bus.'

readingTexts.title: When Japanese is difficult
readingTexts.description: Practice the language used to keep a conversation going when understanding breaks down.

comprehensionQuestions.prompt: What does the speaker ask the other person to do?
choices: Say it again and speak slowly
comprehensionQuestions.answer: Say it again and speak slowly
comprehensionQuestions.explanation: もう一度言ってください and ゆっくり話してください request repetition and slower speech.

comprehensionQuestions.prompt: How much Japanese does the speaker say they understand?
comprehensionQuestions.explanation: はい、少し分かります means 'Yes, I understand a little.'

readingTexts.title: First day at school
readingTexts.description: Read a short sequence about identity, names, friends and Japanese study.

comprehensionQuestions.prompt: What is the speaker?
comprehensionQuestions.explanation: 学生です identifies the speaker as a student.

comprehensionQuestions.prompt: What language do they speak at school?
comprehensionQuestions.explanation: 学校で日本語を話します says they speak Japanese at school.

readingTexts.title: Yesterday and today
readingTexts.description: Bridge into longer comparison across past, negative and present descriptions.

comprehensionQuestions.prompt: What was the weather like yesterday?
comprehensionQuestions.explanation: 昨日は暑かったです says it was hot yesterday.

comprehensionQuestions.prompt: Did the speaker study yesterday?
comprehensionQuestions.explanation: 昨日は勉強しませんでした is the polite past negative: the speaker did not study.

readingTexts.title: Things at home
readingTexts.description: A longer low-support bridge text using possession, existence, description and preference.

comprehensionQuestions.prompt: What is in the house?
comprehensionQuestions.explanation: 家に本があります says there is a book at home.

comprehensionQuestions.prompt: What does the speaker like?
comprehensionQuestions.explanation: 本が好きです means 'I like books.'

readingTexts.title: Weekend plans
readingTexts.description: A short exchange about intentions, scheduled activities and invitations.

comprehensionQuestions.prompt: Which statement appears in "Weekend plans"?
choices: I intend to travel to Kyoto next week.
The speaker buys a new car.
comprehensionQuestions.answer: I intend to travel to Kyoto next week.
comprehensionQuestions.explanation: The text includes: 来週、京都へ旅行するつもりです。 — I intend to travel to Kyoto next week.

comprehensionQuestions.prompt: Which idea appears near the end of the text?
comprehensionQuestions.explanation: Near the end: 日本に行ったことがあります。 — I have been to Japan.
